trials.hypothesis: The observed target is shifted by X/2 columns in x. Joining obs with a copy shifted by X/2 in x (done only by slicing and concatenation) puts the target and build in the same frame within reach of a 1x1 layer, whichever channels are shifted. Expect clearly nonzero dev success and episodes longer than 1. If success stays near 0 with DONE-only behaviour, the misalignment idea is refuted.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


def xroll(t, s):
    if s <= 0:
        return t
    return torch.cat([t[..., -s:], t[..., :-s]], dim=-1)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2
        cin = 2 * spec.in_channels
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        o = torch.cat([obs, xroll(obs, self.shift)], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(o)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.name: learned circular row conv
trials.hypothesis: Add a learned circular 1xX convolution beside the 1x1 stem. Each cell then sees its whole row at every x-offset, so the network can learn the X/2 shift (or any shift) without a hand-coded roll. This tests whether a general learned global-x layer recovers the alignment. Refuted if dev success stays near 0 while the dual-frame candidate succeeds, or if both fail.

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

        res = []

                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        X = int(spec.X)
        self.X = X
        self.left = X // 2
        self.right = X - 1 - self.left
        self.s1 = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1)
        self.wide = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, (1, X))
        self.s2 = nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        X = self.X
        parts = []
        if self.left > 0:
            parts.append(obs[..., X - self.left:])
        parts.append(obs)
        if self.right > 0:
            parts.append(obs[..., :self.right])
        p = torch.cat(parts, dim=-1)
        h = F.relu(self.s1(obs) + self.wide(p))
        s = F.relu(self.s2(h))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)

    return Net(spec)

import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {'ppo_epochs': 2, 'n_envs': 256, 'rollout_len': 16, 'n_minibatches': 16, 'ent_coef': 0.015}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


def xroll(t, s):
    if s <= 0:
        return t
    return torch.cat([t[..., -s:], t[..., :-s]], dim=-1)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2
        cin = 2 * spec.in_channels
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=2, dilation=2)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        o = torch.cat([obs, xroll(obs, self.shift)], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(o)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))

import torch

import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


def xroll(t, s):
    if s <= 0:
        return t
    return torch.cat([t[..., -s:], t[..., :-s]], dim=-1)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))

        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        o = torch.cat([obs, xroll(obs, self.shift)], dim=1)

        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {'ppo_epochs': 1, 'n_envs': 256, 'rollout_len': 16, 'n_minibatches': 16, 'ent_coef': 0.015, 'gamma': 0.99, 'gae_lambda': 0.95}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


def xroll(t, s):
    if s <= 0:
        return t
    return torch.cat([t[..., -s:], t[..., :-s]], dim=-1)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2
        cin = 2 * spec.in_channels
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        o = torch.cat([obs, xroll(obs, self.shift)], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(o)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: The starting network learned to press DONE at once (episode length 1.0, success 0), so no evidence about architectures exists yet. The traces show a key clue: the target heights the agent observes are the design cyclically shifted by 4 = X/2 columns in x (row 1: 00220000 shows as 00000022; row 6: 00000010 shows as 00100000; the same shift fits all rows of design 2). Rewards and actions use world coordinates. A 2-layer 3x3 CNN (receptive field ±2) cannot match the target to the build or the actions across a 4-column shift, so every placement looks random and costly, and DONE is the rational choice. The fixes are to align the frames: (A) feed the network copies of the channels both unshifted and shifted by X/2, or (B) a learned circular 1xX convolution that can learn any x-shift. (C) adds a cheaper recipe with more updates and more entropy to fix (A).
analyses.2: The starting network was misaligned: the observed target is shifted by X/2 columns, and every placement looked wrong to it, so it learned to press DONE at once. Feeding the network the observation next to a copy rolled by X/2 fixed this (r1c1: 0.59, seeds 0.48 and 0.70). A learned 1xX circular convolution also learned the shift but scored lower (0.35). The lean recipe (2 PPO epochs, 128 environments, ent 0.02) learned much faster on seed 0 (0.65 dev, 0.59 train) but its other seed failed completely (0.0). So more samples look valuable, but the small batch was unstable. Under the default recipe, training success was still rising steeply at the end, so the agent is short of samples. The traces show the agent pressing DONE too early with target cells still missing (design 1), and trouble with stacked or overhanging columns. Both point to weak global and ordering reasoning.
analyses.3: The observed target is shifted by X/2 columns in x. Adding a rolled copy of the input (dual-frame) fixes this: success went from 0 to 0.59. Cutting PPO epochs from 4 to 2 while keeping 256 envs nearly doubled the samples, and success rose to 0.79 (seeds 0.78 and 0.80), the clearest gain beyond noise so far. Training success was still rising steeply at the end (0.39 to 0.71 over the last half), so the agent is short of samples. Two additions to r2c1 scored much lower: a dilated third conv (0.11) and a global broadcast (0.24). Both mostly failed by choosing DONE too early with the upper layers still missing. Seed spread is large (up to 0.3), but neither result is close. Extra capacity or extra paths have not helped yet. The best bets are recipe changes: more samples (1 epoch), and a longer reward horizon so the +1 exact-build bonus reaches early ordering choices and discourages early DONE.
analyses.4: The observed target is shifted by X/2 in x. Adding a rolled copy of the input (dual-frame) fixes this: dev success went from 0 to 0.59. The learned circular row conv also worked but scored lower (0.35). Cutting PPO epochs from 4 to 2 at 256 envs gave the best result so far (r2c1, 0.79, both seeds close). Most failures look like seeds collapsing to DONE-only. That happened with 1 epoch (0.21/0.00), with gamma 0.99 (0.00/0.32 and 0.00/0.00), and in one seed with 128 envs. The sign is consistent: a longer horizon makes it look worse to keep placing randomly than to stop, and more frequent noisy updates lock in that choice. The two architecture additions (dilated conv, global broadcast) scored lower, partly through fewer samples and partly through seed luck. For the last round, I keep the r2c1 network and recipe and change one thing per trial to make collapse less likely: shorter horizon, more entropy, or near-uniform output initialisation.
